Out of scope items keep an ID for the same reason requirements do. They get quoted in status calls.
column3: What was asked for, in the words it was asked in.

column3: Why it is not in this scope

red: Recognise the same person across their phone, laptop and tablet
column3: This needs an identity decision and a consent decision before it needs an analytics decision. Neither has been made, and making them inside an implementation project would make the project late.
column4: A signed identity and consent position, then a separate piece of work using the identity service.

red: Include orders taken by the call centre
column3: There is no web interaction to measure. These orders exist only in the order system.
column4: A scheduled import of offline orders, matched on order ID.

red: Export a list of customers who abandoned a cart, so marketing can email them
column3: Individual customer records are not what this platform is for, and the consent position does not currently allow it.
column4: An audience platform, plus a consent basis that covers it.

red: Reconcile website revenue with the finance ledger to the penny
column3: Analytics counts what a browser managed to send. Finance counts what the bank settled. They will never agree, and treating one as the book of record for the other creates work that never ends.
column4: Nothing. This is the wrong tool for that question, and the order system remains the book of record.

red: Build a delivery cost calculator on the product page
column3: This is a website feature and not an analytics requirement. It is recorded here so that it reaches the right team rather than being lost.
column4: A request to the website product team. Once built, tracking it is a small change request.

red: Track the iOS and Android applications
column3: The applications are on a separate release cycle and have no data layer. Bringing them into this phase would put the website date at risk.
column4: A separate mobile implementation, once the applications are ready.
